subject: creatinine
correct: After starting/increasing an ACEi/ARB: do not change the dose if eGFR falls <25% or creatinine rises <30%; if eGFR falls >=25% or creatinine rises >=30%, look for other causes (volume depletion, NSAIDs) and reduce or stop if none (NICE NG203 1.6; NG136). The site's tools/prescribing, CKD, hypertension and proteinuria pages already use 30%/25%.

fixes.old: Creatinine rise >25% or eGFR fall >25% → hold ACEi/ARB
fixes.new: Creatinine rise ≥30% or eGFR fall ≥25% → look for other causes; reduce or stop ACEi/ARB if none

fixes.old: Creatinine rise >25% → hold ACEi; check dehydration.
fixes.new: Creatinine rise ≥30% (or eGFR fall ≥25%) → check dehydration and other causes; reduce or stop ACEi if none.

fixes.old: Creatinine ↑ >25% → hold; investigate RAS.
fixes.new: Creatinine ↑ ≥30% (or eGFR ↓ ≥25%) → look for other causes; reduce or stop if none; consider RAS.

fixes.old: nephrology input if creatinine rises >25% or K⁺ >5.5
fixes.new: nephrology input if creatinine rises ≥30% (or eGFR falls ≥25%) or K⁺ >5.5

fixes.old: stop if K⁺ >6.0 or creatinine rises >25%
fixes.new: stop if K⁺ ≥6.0; if creatinine rises ≥30% (or eGFR falls ≥25%), look for other causes and reduce or stop if none

fixes.old: Creatinine ↑ >25% → hold ACEi; investigate renal artery stenosis.
fixes.new: Creatinine ↑ ≥30% (or eGFR ↓ ≥25%) → look for other causes; reduce or stop ACEi if none; consider renal artery stenosis.

fixes.old: (<20–25% from baseline = acceptable; >30%: investigate; stop if severe)
fixes.new: (rise <30% from baseline, or eGFR fall <25%, = acceptable; ≥30%: investigate other causes; reduce or stop if none)

fixes.new: suspect if creatinine rises ≥30% on an ACEi

fixes.old: suspect if creatinine jumps >25% on an ACEi
fixes.new: suspect if creatinine rises ≥30% on an ACEi

fixes.old: A ≤25% creatinine rise is expected and acceptable.
fixes.new: A creatinine rise of less than 30% (eGFR fall of less than 25%) is expected and acceptable.

fixes.new: don’t stop for a rise of less than 30% (NICE NG203).

fixes.new: Expect a small creatinine rise (less than 30%; eGFR fall less than 25%)

note: Several cases use '>25% creatinine rise -> hold', mixing up the NG203 eGFR (25%) and creatinine (30%) thresholds. Legitimate and left unchanged: cases/eczema.html (ciclosporin, >25% above baseline -> reduce dose, per BAD/SPC) and cases/heart-failure.html (>50% on ACEi, the HF practical-guidance tolerance). The owner may still want to align the HF page with its own '>30% -> stop + specialist' wording.

subject: gabapentin
correct: Gabapentin SPC renal dosing uses creatinine clearance: CrCl 50–79 = 600–1,800 mg/day; 30–49 = 300–900 mg/day; 15–29 = 150–600 mg/day; <15 = 150–300 mg/day. Reduce from CrCl <80. Pregabalin is reduced from CrCl <60.

fixes.old: gabapentin maximum 900mg/day at eGFR 30–59
fixes.new: gabapentin maximum 1,800mg/day at CrCl 50–79 and 900mg/day at CrCl 30–49 (SPC)

fixes.old: Gabapentin/pregabalin: reduce at eGFR <30
fixes.new: Gabapentin: reduce at CrCl <80; pregabalin: reduce at CrCl <60 (SPC)

note: The 900 mg cap applies only at CrCl 30–49. At 50–59 the maximum is 1,800 mg/day, so the case under-states the dose for part of the band. The CKD case says gabapentinoids need reducing only below eGFR 30, which is unsafe: dose reduction starts much earlier. The pregabalin band table in cases/neuropathic-pain.html matches its SPC and is left unchanged.

subject: morphine
correct: Opioids Aware (FPM, updated): threshold lowered from 120 to 90 mg/day oral morphine equivalent, with about 50 mg/day as the ideal/heightened-review level. Seek specialist advice above 90 mg/day.

fixes.old: Review regularly; above about 120 mg oral morphine equivalent a day, harms rise without added benefit (Opioids Aware, FPM)
fixes.new: Review regularly; treat about 50 mg/day oral morphine equivalent as a prompt for heightened review and seek specialist advice before exceeding 90 mg/day: above this, harms rise without added benefit (Opioids Aware, FPM 2026)

note: Every other page (hip-pain, neck-pain, analgesia-primary-care, opioid-prescribing, sca-addons-7) already uses 50/90. tools/prescribing.html still has the superseded 120 mg figure.

subject: morphine
group: dose | mg (IM morphine in suspected ACS)
correct: Suspected ACS/MI: offer pain relief as soon as possible with GTN, and offer IV opioids such as morphine, particularly if MI is suspected (NICE CG95). Avoid IM injections in suspected MI: absorption is erratic and haematoma risk is high with antithrombotic or thrombolytic treatment. In primary care without IV access, leave opioid analgesia to the ambulance crew.

fixes.old: • Morphine 5–10mg IM for severe pain pending ambulance (caution: reduces clopidogrel absorption).
fixes.new: • Severe pain not relieved by GTN: IV opioid (e.g. morphine, titrated) with an antiemetic if IV access is available; avoid IM injections in suspected MI (NICE CG95). Otherwise leave analgesia to the ambulance crew (caution: opioids delay oral P2Y12 absorption).

fixes.old: Morphine sulphate 5–10mg IM/IV / Diamorphine 2.5–5mg IV (hospital)
fixes.new: Morphine sulphate 5–10mg IV, slow and titrated (avoid IM in suspected MI) / Diamorphine 2.5–5mg IV (hospital)

fixes.old: 5–10mg IM titrated
fixes.new: 5–10mg IV titrated

fixes.old: Morphine IM for severe pain + antiemetic
fixes.new: IV opioid (not IM) + antiemetic for severe pain if IV access; otherwise leave to the ambulance crew

fixes.old: Morphine IM for pain relief is appropriate.
fixes.new: IV opioid for pain relief if IV access is available (avoid IM injections).

note: CG95 wording comes from established guidance. nice.org.uk could not be opened directly in this pass, so the fixing pass should spot-check it. The last fix (suspected aortic dissection row) is the same principle: avoid IM injections when anticoagulation or surgery may follow.

subject: levothyroxine
correct: On a positive pregnancy test, empirically increase levothyroxine by about 25–30%, e.g. two extra doses a week (~29%). Then titrate to TSH/FT4; some women eventually need 30–50% more. The 20–30% wording (ATA/THERAPY trial) is the same practical rule.

fixes.new: levothyroxine ↑25–30% at positive test · ptu

note: The dedicated thyroid-pregnancy page, the hypothyroidism case and the summaries give 25–30% as the immediate step, and say only that 'some women need 30–50%' later. The search-card taglines and the meds file present 30–50% / 25–50% as the immediate increase. The RCOG 2025 GTG text could not be opened. The 20–30% wording in abnormal-tfts.html, one-page/abnormal-tfts.html, sca-cases11.js and thyroid-hypo-young.json is clinically equivalent ('two extra doses a week'). The owner may optionally standardise it to 25–30%, but no change is required.

subject: levothyroxine
correct: In older people, start 25–50 micrograms and titrate in 25 microgram steps. Recheck TSH no sooner than 6–8 weeks after each change (NG145: about every 3 months until stable). Aim for TSH within the reference range; a higher target is often appropriate in older adults. There is no NG145 target of 0.5–2.5.

fixes.old: titrate to TSH 0.5–2.5)
fixes.new: titrate to a TSH within the reference range; a higher target may suit older people)

fixes.old: titrate up by 25mcg every 4 weeks to TSH 0.5–2.5)
fixes.new: titrate in 25mcg steps, rechecking TSH no sooner than 6–8 weeks after each change, aiming for TSH within the reference range)

note: Titrating every 4 weeks is faster than TSH can equilibrate. A 0.5–2.5 target risks over-replacement in older people with dementia. 0.5–2.5 is a pre-conception/pregnancy target used elsewhere on the site.

subject: rivaroxaban
correct: Rivaroxaban AF: 20 mg OD with food; 15 mg OD if CrCl 15–49; not recommended if CrCl <15. Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD (COMPASS): no dose adjustment; caution at CrCl 15–29; not recommended <15. Apixaban AF reduction applies at CrCl 15–29 or with 2 of age/weight/creatinine. Edoxaban reduction applies at CrCl 15–50.

fixes.old: Rivaroxaban 20 mg OD with food (15 mg at the CrCl threshold)
fixes.new: Rivaroxaban 20 mg OD with food (15 mg OD if CrCl 15–49)

fixes.old: CrCl <30 → dose adjustment or switch.
fixes.new: CrCl <50 → check product-specific dose reduction (rivaroxaban 15 mg if CrCl 15–49; edoxaban 30 mg if 15–50; apixaban per SPC criteria).

fixes.old: Annual renal function (rivaroxaban dose-adjustment at CrCl <15)
fixes.new: Annual renal function (rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD: no dose change, use with caution at CrCl 15–29, avoid below 15)

note: The tia-stroke monitoring table implies no DOAC change until CrCl <30, which misses rivaroxaban/edoxaban reductions from CrCl <50. The PAD page wrongly describes a 'dose adjustment at CrCl <15' for the COMPASS dose. The site's AF and anticoagulant management pages already use the correct values.

subject: emollient/steroid cream
correct: On an infant's face use mild potency only (hydrocortisone). Moderate-potency betamethasone valerate 0.025% is for the body, not the face, without specialist advice (NICE CG57). The same page already says '(body; avoid face)'.

fixes.old: stronger topical CS (HC 2.5% or betamethasone 0.025% face)
fixes.new: stronger topical CS (HC 2.5% for the face; betamethasone valerate 0.025% for the body only, not the face)

note: Line 278 of cases/cmpa-reflux.html suggests betamethasone 0.025% on the face of an infant. Lines 534/538 of the same page say avoid face.
